text:
The emotional high point of Kaapo Kakko's season came in Finland, where NHL.com wrote that the Global Series game in his home country was special to him "despite loss." In Seattle, he is a playmaker first, with 13 points (10 assists) in 19 games at about 14 minutes a night.

The shot count is the oddity. He has 18 shots in 19 games, and his own chances add up to just 2.04 expected goals (the quality of chances). Nearly all of his value is in setting others up, which Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs up: last season 19% of his setups came from behind the net (8% for a typical forward), and he exited the zone with control 67% of the time.

Some caution on the points. The Kraken have scored 7.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and they trail on five-on-five expected goals (46%) when he plays. Evolving-Hockey liked him a lot last season (73rd of 401 forwards, despite weak linemates), so the talent is not the question. Alison Lukan, a Kraken contributor, posted that the "Kakko-Beniers-Samo line also cooked" in a recent 5-1 win.
